definitions.gloss: zero points; zero marks; a score of zero
definitions.explanation: A score of zero on a test, exam, or evaluation. Also used figuratively to mean something is completely unacceptable or worthless.

examples.japanese: テストで{零点|れいてん}を{取|と}った。
examples.english: I got zero on the test.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}を{書|か}き{忘|わす}れたら{零点|れいてん}になる。
examples.english: If you forget to write your name, you'll get zero points.

examples.japanese: マナーに{関|かん}しては{零点|れいてん}だが、{仕事|しごと}の{腕|うで}は{確|たし}かだ。
examples.english: His manners are a zero, but his work skills are solid.

notes:
Most commonly associated with academic tests and exams. Also used figuratively as a harsh evaluation meaning "completely failing" in some area. The kanji {零|れい} is the formal character for zero.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {零点|れいてん}を{取|と}る: to get zero points
- {零点|れいてん}をつける: to give zero points
- {零点|れいてん}になる: to end up with zero

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ゼロ{点|てん}: zero points — uses the loanword ゼロ; more casual
- {満点|まんてん}: perfect score — the opposite, getting all points
- {赤点|あかてん}: failing mark — a score below the passing threshold, but not necessarily zero
